players.product: CMP pads & slurries, photoresists, advanced-packaging laminates (ex-DuPont Electronics)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 net sales $1.4 billion, up 22% year-over-year and 9% sequentially (organic +22%); adjusted operating EBITDA $431 million, up 24%, margin 30.2%; adjusted EPS $1.19, up 53%; ninth consecutive quarter of profitable organic growth; adjusted free cash flow $259 million.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales $1.4 billion (+22% YoY, +9% QoQ); adj. EBITDA $431 million (30.2%); adj. EPS $1.19 (+53%)

quarterly_data.signal: Interconnect Solutions (ICS) net sales $685 million, up more than 30% year-over-year and 16% sequentially, organic +28%, led by the three growth platforms of advanced packaging and interconnect, AI PCBs and thermal management, which collectively grew more than 50% year-over-year again; ICS gross margin ~44%, adjusted EBITDA margin ~29%, up 290 basis points YoY, now viewed as structurally in the high 20% range.
quarterly_data.figure: ICS $685 million (+30% YoY, +16% QoQ); AI growth platforms +50% YoY; ICS EBITDA margin ~29%

quarterly_data.signal: New advanced packaging architectures (panel-level packaging, larger package formats, tighter lines and spaces on high-layer-count boards and IC substrates) all mean more material complexity and more material intensity, with fewer suppliers able to qualify; Qnity has incumbency with the same customers that commercialized the existing advanced packaging formats and expects more content per package as formats grow. Customer capacity expansions in advanced packaging underpin the durability of ICS growth.

Winning new business in pulse plating, a key metallization technology for the most advanced high-layer-count printed circuit boards used in AI applications (density, signal integrity, power delivery); thermal portfolio broadened to liquid thermal interface materials, phase change materials, thermal pads and gap fillers for AI systems and data center infrastructure.

Full-year 2026 guidance raised: net sales $5.55 billion-$5.65 billion, adjusted operating EBITDA $1.675 billion-$1.725 billion, adjusted EPS $4.40-$4.60, adjusted free cash flow $600 million-$700 million; at the midpoint 18% net sales growth, over 20% adjusted EBITDA growth and 35% adjusted EPS growth. Q3: sequential net sales growth in the low single digits overall (ICS mid-single digits with high-20s EBITDA margin; semi low single digits with mid-30s margin).
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 net sales $5.55 billion-$5.65 billion (+18% at midpoint); adj. EBITDA $1.675 billion-$1.725 billion; adj. EPS $4.40-$4.60

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: approximately $600 million of growth investments deployed since 2022 under the local-for-local model, mostly quick modular expansions in step with customer roadmaps; capex $90 million in the quarter, elevated for the full year, returning to the 6% of net sales range longer term. Management says growth is faster than expected but it can bring capacity online quickly and is well prepared for 2027 and 2028; no near-term risk to supply or output from the ~$20 million logistics/energy cost pressure, which is being offset by targeted pricing.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$600 million growth investment since 2022; capex $90 million in Q2; ~$20 million cost headwind

quarterly_data.signal: Portfolio mix: advanced logic and logic roughly 80%, memory about 20% with HBM and DRAM growing a little faster (ticked up a couple of percentage points); by end market data centers ticked up, industrial markets (automotive, aerospace and defense, telecom infrastructure) steady, consumer electronics growing slower. AI data centers carry a very strong margin profile because of the advanced-technology content.

Industry volume indicators: MSI expected in the high single digits for 2026 and PCB growth in the mid to high single digits; Qnity content outperformance sits considerably above the MSI benchmark because all logic and memory leaders are successfully commercializing their most advanced nodes at once.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 MSI high single digits; PCB growth mid to high single digits

players.product: CMP pads, cleans & slurries and lithography ancillary materials for leading-edge logic/memory (ex-DuPont Electronics)

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor Technologies net sales $744 million, up approximately 3% sequentially and 17% organically year-over-year, driven by demand strength especially for advanced logic and HBM chips; semi gross margin ~49% and adjusted operating EBITDA margin ~34% (right around 35% for the first half, expected to continue).
quarterly_data.figure: Semiconductor Technologies $744 million (+17% organic YoY); EBITDA margin ~34%

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced nodes portfolio grew more than 20% in Q2 (Investor Day plan was ~7%): continued growth at three nanometer, emerging activity at two nanometer, really strong pull for 2 nm and 18A, and successful scale-up of HBM3/HBM4 on the memory side; advanced nodes were about 40% of the portfolio exiting the first half versus the 45%-50% Investor Day target, which Qnity expects to reach early.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced nodes +20% YoY; ~40% of portfolio vs 45%-50% target

quarterly_data.signal: Fab utilization: advanced logic tracking to the mid-80% range, mainstream logic low 80%, DRAM high 80%, NAND low 80%; every wafer at advanced nodes requires more layers, more processing complexity and more packaging steps, translating to more Qnity content.
quarterly_data.figure: utilization: advanced logic mid-80%, mainstream logic low 80%, DRAM high 80%, NAND low 80%

quarterly_data.signal: CMP is the fastest-growing part of the semi portfolio (pads, cleans and slurries) with the most content gains plus incremental share gains on cleans and slurries; launched the Optivision Max soft polishing pad, already adopted at leading-edge nodes and in advanced packaging including AI and HBM-driven architectures; multiple POR wins at 16 and 14 (angstrom-era nodes) in the first half.

Lithography materials business continues to do really well; for the Qnity portfolio EUV matters less in the photoresist layer than in the ancillary layers around the photoresist, where it partners with customers to get the most out of their EUV investment. Kalrez (perfluoroelastomer seals) saw strong first-half growth on accelerated wafer fab equipment demand and is getting productivity, capacity release and automation initiatives.

Qnity is a consumables business correlated to wafer volume; MSI expected in the high single digits for 2026, with content outperformance considerably above MSI as all logic and memory leaders commercialize their most advanced technology simultaneously.
